result.topic_en: Euler computes the variation arising from the boundary (second) part of the integral when the neighbouring curve passes through the initial endpoint A but ends at a different point μ or ω, and begins to determine the angle between the chord Mω and the principal curve.
result.transcription:
VARIATIONVM TRACTANDI. 59
vnice ad vltimum terminum M, vbi $dt\left(\frac{dy}{dt}\right)$ ipſum
ſpatiolum M$\mu$ exprimit, ſimilique modo in alte-
ram partem pro initio A ſpatiolum A$\alpha$ ingredie-
tur. Hinc patet ſi omnes curuae proximae $\alpha\mu$
per ipſos ambos terminos A et M ducantur tum
variationem ſecundae partis in nihilum abire.

40. Conſideremus autem caſum, quo curua
proxima $\alpha\mu$ per primum quidem terminum A tran-
ſit non vero quoque per alterum M, ſed ſit pun-
ctum $\mu$ eius terminus, atque variatio ex ſecunda
parte nata erit
$= M\mu\left(P - \frac{dQ}{dx} + \frac{ddR}{dx^2}\text{ etc.}\right).$
Atque hinc etiam definire poterimus variationem ex
eodem fonte oriundam, ſi curua proxima A$\mu$, non
in ipſo puncto $\mu$ ſed alio quocunque $\omega$ terminetur, ex-
iſtente ſemper interuallo $\mu\omega$ infinite paruo. Ducta
enim applicata $\omega m p$, variatio modo inuenta inſuper
augeri debet particula formulae $\int Z\,dx$, quae ele-
mento $Pp = dx$ reſpondet, quae particula quum ſit
$= Z.\,Pp$, pro arcu curuae proximae A$\omega$ erit va-
riatio ex ſecunda parte oriunda
$= M\mu\left(P - \frac{dQ}{dx} + \frac{ddR}{dx^2}\text{ etc.}\right) + Z.\,Pp.$

41. Ducatur recta M$\omega$ et quaeramus angu-
lum $\omega$M$m$, quem haec recta M$\omega$ cum curua prin-
cipali conſtituit, ponatur iſte angulus $\omega$M$m = \omega$
et ducta MO ipſi P$p$ parallela, quia eſt proxime
$m\omega = M\mu$ et anguli $m$M$o$ tangens $= p$ ideoque
H 2 om

items.quote:
Hinc patet ſi omnes curuae proximae $\alpha\mu$
per ipſos ambos terminos A et M ducantur tum
variationem ſecundae partis in nihilum abire.
items.english: Hence it is clear that if all neighbouring curves αμ are drawn through both endpoints A and M themselves, then the variation of the second part vanishes.

items.quote:
Atque hinc etiam definire poterimus variationem ex
eodem fonte oriundam, ſi curua proxima A$\mu$, non
in ipſo puncto $\mu$ ſed alio quocunque $\omega$ terminetur
items.english: And from this we can also determine the variation arising from the same source if the neighbouring curve Aμ ends not at the point μ itself but at any other point ω.

items.quote:
Ducatur recta M$\omega$ et quaeramus angu-
lum $\omega$M$m$, quem haec recta M$\omega$ cum curua prin-
cipali conſtituit
items.english: Let the straight line Mω be drawn and let us seek the angle ωMm which this line Mω makes with the principal curve.
